misconceptions.description: Selecting portfolio artifacts by grade, polish, or recency rather than by the competency they evidence
misconceptions.trigger: learner chooses the highest-scoring or newest assignments without matching them to a claim
misconceptions.feedback: Start from the competency claim, then choose the artifact that best evidences it, even if its grade was lower.

misconceptions.description: Including artifacts with no statement of which standard they evidence or how
misconceptions.trigger: artifact appears in the portfolio with no rationale tag
misconceptions.feedback: Add a rationale that names the competency the artifact supports and the evidence inside it that shows the claim.

misconceptions.description: Treating an AI ranking as the curatorial decision rather than as input the teacher must judge against the rubric
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts the model's recommended set without checking it against the actual standards
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI to cluster candidate evidence, then make the final selection yourself against the rubric.

misconceptions.description: Believing only flawless work belongs in a portfolio, so reflective growth artifacts are cut
misconceptions.trigger: learner removes an artifact because it documents a lesson that went poorly
misconceptions.feedback: A documented revision can evidence reflective judgment; keep it if its rationale names what the growth shows.
